article.title: Chandrashekar et al. (2020), Genetic population structure of endangered ring-tailed lemurs (Lemur catta) from nine sites in southern Madagascar
article.version: Ecology and Evolution 10(15):8030-8043; version of record first published 2020-07-16
article.locator: Abstract; Methods 2.1 Sample collection and Table 1; Results 3.2 Population genetic structure; Discussion 4.1 Genetic diversity and population structure
article.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), item-level license stated by Crossref and the article's Creative Commons Attribution notice
article.scope: Primary population-genetic study using multilocus genotypes from 106 adult ring-tailed lemurs at nine localities in southern Madagascar. Claims are paraphrased and bounded to those samples, markers, analyses and collection period. No figures, tables, datasets or supplementary files are reproduced.
article.licenseAppliesTo: The published article text; no third-party material or supplementary dataset is reused.

evolution.text: The study's multilocus analyses found moderate genetic differentiation among sampled localities, with geographically structured northern, southern, western and potentially central clusters. This describes population structure inferred from the study's markers and nine sites; it is not a species-level phylogeny or a complete evolutionary history.
evolution.scope: 106 adult individuals sampled at nine geographically representative localities; analyses and marker set reported in the 2020 study.

distribution.text: The paper sampled nine localities across the authors' stated existing range in southern Madagascar, including northeastern, central, southeastern and western sites. The locality list is a study sample and does not establish a complete or current range boundary.
distribution.locator: Methods 2.1 Sample collection and Table 1; Figure 2
distribution.scope: Locality records selected for the 2020 study; not an exhaustive occurrence inventory.

article.title: Holzner et al. (2021), Occupancy of wild southern pig-tailed macaques in intact and degraded forests in Peninsular Malaysia
article.locator: Abstract; Methods Study sites, Detection histories and Occupancy modelling; Results; Discussion
article.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), item-level license stated on the PeerJ article and PMC record
article.scope: Primary camera-trap occupancy study at Pasoh Forest Reserve and Belum-Temengor Forest Complex in Peninsular Malaysia, comparing temporal and spatial patterns under clear-cutting, selective logging and undisturbed conditions. Claims retain the study's site and model limits. No location data, tables, figures or supplementary files are reproduced.
article.licenseAppliesTo: Published article text; no restricted site-location data or third-party material is reused.
article.attribution: Holzner A, Rayan DM, Moore J, Tan CKW, Clart L, Kulik L, Kühl H, Ruppert N, Widdig A (2021). Occupancy of wild southern pig-tailed macaques in intact and degraded forests in Peninsular Malaysia. PeerJ 9:e12462. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.12462. Claims paraphrased under CC BY 4.0.

ecology.text: Camera-trap occupancy estimates indicated that clear-cutting increased local-extinction probability in the Pasoh Forest Reserve model, while the study detected no clear occupancy difference between selectively logged and undisturbed areas in the Belum-Temengor Forest Complex. These findings concern the sampled sites and fitted models, not a range-wide response.
ecology.scope: Pasoh Forest Reserve temporal survey (2013-2017) and Belum-Temengor spatial comparison as modeled in the 2021 study.
ecology.lifeStatus: Wild camera-trap detections and occupancy estimates.

distribution.text: The study documents detections and modeled site occupancy at Pasoh Forest Reserve and Belum-Temengor Forest Complex in Peninsular Malaysia. These are research sites, not a complete distribution statement for the species.
distribution.locator: Methods Study sites; Figure 1; Detection histories
distribution.scope: Two study landscapes and their analyzed camera locations only.
